eeg_analysis_method: Event-related potentials (ERPs) were computed for successful and failed stops, mapping the N1 at FCz and the stop P3 at Cz. Topographical mapping and single bilateral dipole source modeling were conducted using BESA 2.2
epoch segment: −100 to 1552 ms relative to S1/S2

online reference: Recorded with a CPz reference and re-referenced offline to a common-average reference
eeg_analysis_method: Preprocessing using Computational Testing Automated Preprocessing (CTAP) toolbox based on EEGLAB; re-referencing to average mastoids; filtering (2 Hz high-pass, 45 Hz low-pass); blink detection via CTAP; decomposition using FastICA; artifact rejection using FASTER toolbox and manual inspection; Time-Frequency Representations (TFRs) calculated using Morlet wavelets
epoch segment: 2048 ms epochs (CTAP processing)
other information: Automated FASTER toolbox (thresholds based on exceeding ±3 SD of mean channel variance) plus visual inspection

eeg_analysis_method: Spectral Power Analysis: Using Brain Vision Analyzer 2, Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) was applied to 2048 ms non-overlapping Hanning-windowed epochs, yielding a frequency resolution of 0.5 Hz. Relative alpha power (8–12 Hz) was calculated by dividing absolute alpha power by the full spectrum power (1.5 to 40 Hz) and averaged across all 64 electrodes. For topographical analysis, the EEG was filtered with a 0.5 to 40 Hz band-pass filter and a 55–65 Hz notch filter using the Neurophysiological Biomarker Toolbox (NBT); Event-Related Desynchronization (ERD) Analysis: For the Continuous Performance Task (CPT), EEG data was segmented into 1900 ms epochs (beginning 800 ms before stimulus onset) for correct Go and NoGo trials. A time-frequency analysis using a continuum wavelet transform (complex Morlet's wavelets) was applied from 1 to 30 Hz in 1-Hz steps. Alpha ERD amplitude (8–12 Hz) was calculated relative to a pre-stimulus baseline (-800 to -100 ms) and averaged over 28 posterior electrode
other information: Automated FASTER toolbox (thresholds based on exceeding ±3 SD of mean channel variance)

eeg_analysis_method: baseline correction, locked on letter onset epochs
epoch segment: −800 to 800 ms relative to button press/feedback
other information: Automated rejection of epochs with voltage steps >50 μV/ms or absolute deflections exceeding ±100 μV

eeg_analysis_method: baseline correction, grand average wave form, Each component was identified in the grand average difference waveform and analyzed at the sites and latencies of their peak activity (Luck, 2014). Hence, Ne was scored at median frontocentral (FC1, FCz, FC2) and central (C1, Cz, C2) electrodes, between –20 and 100 ms around time point 0. Pe was scored at median central (C1, Cz, C2) and centroparietal (CP1, CPz, CP2) electrodes, between 60 and 500 ms following time-point 0.
epoch segment: −200 to 1500 ms relative to S1 and S2

eeg_analysis_method: Amplitudes of the ERP maps were calculated as global field power (GFP), which measures the root mean square of all voltages in a map to reflect overall map strength. Microstates were identified through adaptive segmentation of the grand mean across groups and conditions. Additionally, automatic peak amplitude and latency detection was employed specifically for the Cue P300 and NoGo P300 components

baseline correction interval: −1000 to 0 ms (−1000 to −900 ms for phase)
other information: Automated FASTER toolbox (thresholds based on exceeding ±3 SD of mean channel variance) plus visual inspection

eeg_analysis_method: A partially automatic peak detection algorithm, which was overseen by two experts to correct for edge effects or ambiguous peaks, was used to determine the latency and amplitude of various ERP components. epoch segment: −300 to 1000 ms relative to tone onset

eeg_analysis_method: Independent components were determined for epochs locked to the onset of stimulus and based on similarity in space, time and frequency dimensions. Custom scripts based on EEGLab were used. Even-related spectral pertubations were extracted from ICs

eeg_analysis_method:
LRPs: Measured maximally at the C3/C4 motor cortex electrodes. Amplitude was scored as the average voltage in an early window (152–250 ms) and a late window (252–500 ms) minus the prestimulus baseline. LRP onset latency was scored using a jackknife approach, defined automatically as the first time sample ≤−0.5 μV relative to baseline; P3b (P402) ERPs: Averaged by condition without the LRP subtraction procedure
. It was scored as the mean of the 250–550 ms window, with latency identified as the timing of the largest amplitude within this window

eeg_analysis_method: ERP components were scored as mean amplitudes extracted from specific time windows at target electrodes where the components are known to be prominent (e.g., Cz and Pz for Cue P3 and Go P3; Fz, Cz, and Pz for NoGo P3 and late CNV; Fz and Cz for NoGo N2)
epoch segment: −200 to 1200 ms relative to S1 and S2 onset
other information: Automated rejection of epochs with absolute amplitude >100 μV, slow wave activity >50 μV, or high-frequency noise >35 μV

eeg_analysis_method: CDA was calculated from lateral-posterior sites by subtracting right hemisphere waveforms from left hemisphere waveforms (when cued right), and vice versa, then averaging them. Independent t-tests were performed along a moving window (100 ms length, 50 ms overlap) during the 300–850 ms retention period to find maximal differences, which were then confirmed with ANOVAs. Data were winsorized to 2 standard deviations
epoch segment: −400 to 1000 ms relative to memory array
other information: Automated exclusion of trials with horizontal/vertical eye movements exceeding ±50 μV

eeg_analysis_method: Artifact-free data underwent Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to extract absolute power for "low alpha" (8–10 Hz) and "high alpha" (10–12 Hz). This was used to calculate Laterality Indices (LIs) across left/right electrode pairs
epoch segment: Continuous data parsed into 1024 ms epochs

eeg_analysis_method: Clean data was segmented into 1-second epochs and processed via Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). The core measures extracted were the power asymmetries for "low beta" (12–16 Hz) and "high beta" (16–21 Hz) frequencies across right-left electrode pairs
epoch segment: Continuous data parsed into 1024 ms epochs

online reference: Average of signals recorded separately at each ear lobe
eeg_analysis_method: The artifact-free epochs were then processed using a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) with a 50% overlap and a Hanning Windowing function to generate spectral content at a 1 Hz resolution. Finally, researchers calculated averaged absolute power and specific Asymmetry Indices (AIs)
epoch segment: Continuous data parsed into 1-second epochs
other information: Automated FASTER toolbox (thresholds based on exceeding ±3 SD of mean channel variance) plus visual inspection

eeg_analysis_method: Event-related potential (ERP) difference waves were generated by subtracting the ipsilateral waveforms from the contralateral waveforms relative to the memory targets. Mean waveforms were measured at eight parieto-occipital electrode sites (corresponding to PO7/8) to analyze the N2pc component within a 220–260ms time window and the CDA component within a 400–800ms time window. Additionally, source analysis was performed on the N2pc and CDA using BESA software

eeg_analysis_method: peak-to-peak measures to calculate the amplitude of ERP components within defined latency windows. eeg_analysis_method: Independent Component Analysis (ICA) was used to decompose Event-Related Potentials (ERPs) into stable, functionally different independent components. Because ERP amplitude data were skewed and transformations were unsuccessful, amplitude data were analyzed using Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) with a robust Hubert White sandwich estimator to account for within-subject correlations across tasks. eeg_analysis_method: Event-related potentials (ERPs) and event-related spectral perturbations (ERSPs) evaluated using a hanning-tapered sinusoidal wavelet transform (short-time DFT)

other information: Automated rejection of epochs with voltage steps >50 μV/ms or absolute deflections exceeding ±100 μV

eeg_analysis_method: Segments were averaged to derive event-related potentials (ERPs) for each participant, with analysis restricted to only correct responses (hits) and correct rejections. The P3a component was measured at frontal electrode 11 (comparable to Fz) and the P3b component was measured at parietal electrode 62 (comparable to Pz). The positive peak amplitude and latency within specific time windows (e.g., 160-424 ms for P3a in the respond-to-target task) were identified for each participant and used for analysis

eeg_analysis_method: Analyzed using grand-average waveforms to calculate peak latencies and mean amplitudes within specific time windows: N1 (100–160 ms), N2 (190–270 ms), and P3 (270–500 ms). These were measured at specific fronto-central channels selected after visual inspection (FZ and FCZ for N1; FCZ and CZ for N2 and P3)
epoch segment: −1250 to 1250 ms relative to stimulus onset
other information: Automated FASTER toolbox (thresholds based on exceeding ±3 SD of mean channel variance)

online reference: Cz was used as the internal reference during recording; the data was re-referenced offline to linked mastoids
eeg_analysis_method: EEG was transformed into time–frequency representations (ERSPs) using Morlet wavelets (2–30 Hz). Analyses focused on theta activity (4–8 Hz). Data were segmented into eight overlapping 200-ms time windows from −100 to 800 ms post-stimulus. Theta power was extracted for four sensor-space ROIs: frontal-midline, frontolateral left, frontolateral right, parietal. Power was defined around each participant’s maximum theta peak (±1 Hz, ±50 ms). Functional connectivity was computed using imaginary coherence between five ROI pairs. A surface Laplacian was applied to reduce volume-conduction effects. Trial numbers were balanced across conditions to ensure comparable signal-to-noise ratios.
epoch segment: −100 to 2400 ms relative to stimulus onset

eeg_analysis_method: ERP peak analysis for correct trials. Latency ranges were visually defined as 170–340 ms for the N200 and 300–500 ms for the P300. Local peak amplitudes and latencies were extracted using an automatic detection procedure at midline electrodes Fz, Cz, and Pz, followed by visual checking and manual adjustments if needed
epoch segment: −200 to 1000 ms relative to letter onset
other information: Automated rejection of epochs with voltage steps >50 μV/ms or absolute deflections exceeding ±100 μV

eeg_analysis_method: Iterative independent component analysis (iICA) was used on single-trial evoked potentials. This approach aims to enhance a specific component (like the N2 or P3 peak) by separating statistically independent sources and making the brain responses clearly visible in individual trials despite low signal-to-noise ratios

eeg_analysis_method: Quantitative EEG (QEEG) using Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) on artifact-free 2-second epochs
epoch segment: Continuous data parsed into 2-second epochs

eeg_analysis_method: Event-related potential (ERP) analysis. Lateralized activity for the Contralateral Delay Activity (CDA) was quantified by subtracting ipsilateral from contralateral activity. Mean amplitudes were extracted for defined time windows (e.g., 320–370 ms and 370–700 ms for CDA; 300–600 ms for P3b) at selected electrode clusters
epoch segment: −400 to 1000 ms relative to stimulus onset

other information: Automated FASTER toolbox (thresholds based on exceeding ±3 SD of mean channel variance)

eeg_analysis_method: Event-related potentials (ERPs) were averaged separately for Go and No-Go stimuli. The fronto-central N2 peaks were scored in the 250–400 ms window at Fz and Cz, while the parietal P3 amplitude was defined as the most positive peak in the 300–500 ms window at Pz. The N2 effect was calculated by subtracting the Go N2 amplitude from the No-Go N2 amplitude. Electrodes were (Fz, Cz, Pz, Oz)

eeg_analysis_method: Peak amplitude extraction was used. The ERN amplitude was defined as the largest negative peak in the 30 to 120-ms window after an error, and the Pe amplitude was defined as the maximal positive peak in the 200 to 400-ms interval following an error
epoch segment: −500 to 500 ms relative to response onset

eeg_analysis_method: ERP components during correct Nogo trials were automatically coded and manually checked by blinded research assistants. The N2 component was defined as the largest peak negative deflection between 200 and 400 ms post-stimulus with a frontocentral topography, averaged across sites FCz, Fz, and Cz. The P3 component was measured as the mean activation across parietal sites (Pz, P3, and P4) between 300 and 600 ms post-stimulus. The early occipital P1 and N1 components were scored between 80–160 ms and 130–230 ms post-stimulus, respectively, averaged across sites Oz, O1, and O2. Medication and trial count effects were covaried out of each ERP analysis
epoch segment: −400 to 1000 ms relative to letter onset

eeg_analysis_method: Event-related potential (ERP) analysis only included correct trials. The N1 and P2 components were quantified at the Fz electrode (as well as an averaged cluster of F1, F2, and Fz) using time windows of 40–120 ms and 120–220 ms poststimulus, respectively. The P3 component was quantified at the Pz electrode (and an averaged cluster of P1, P2, Pz) within a 200–500 ms window. Average amplitudes were calculated in a symmetric 50 ms interval around the peak latency for each component
epoch segment: −200 to 1000 ms relative to N-back digit onset
